title: Cancellation is the one governance power Sky is willing to make fully permissionless
content:
Protego exposes two escalation levels. A.1.10.5.3.1.1 describes the narrow one: an **Emergency Drop Spell** is deployed against a specific planned action and, "once authorized by Sky Governance," can cancel it — execution requires the spell to hold the `hat` in the Chief contract. Deployment itself is already open: A.1.10.5.3.1.1.1 notes "any user can permissionlessly deploy an Emergency Drop Spell," so only the authorization step is gated.

The broad one is A.1.10.5.3.1.2: Protego itself "can be granted authority by Sky Governance to allow any user to permissionlessly cancel any planned governance action," again by giving the contract the `hat`. Once granted, A.1.10.5.3.1.2.1 and A.1.10.5.3.1.2.2 let anyone drop a single plan or a batch of plans in one call.

What makes this defensible is the asymmetry of the power. Every other emergency capability in the Atlas can *cause* a state change, so it must be tightly held. Cancellation can only *subtract* pending actions — the worst an attacker with drop authority can do is force governance to re-pass a proposal through the ordinary process. Griefing is possible; theft is not.

The design consequence is a genuine tiering: identify-and-cancel-one requires a vote per target and stays narrow, while switching Protego on wholesale converts the pause delay into a public veto that nobody has to be trusted to exercise. The second is stronger medicine — it makes governance unable to execute anything while it is active — which is why it takes the hat rather than a standing grant.
description: Granted the hat in Chief, Protego lets any user drop any planned action, singly or in batches; Emergency Drop Spells are the narrower alternative, targeting one pre-identified action.
